notes: Sim-computed: metrics, agents, roads, tracts (real polygons + ACS/HOLC equity fields), line, impact.modeSplit, impact.minutesSavedByEarnings, verdict label/headline/summary/grades and all five tests, whoPays.items and whoPays.approval.
Not computed by the sim (copied from the frontend mock): verdict.alternatives, impact.tiles, impact.calibration, claims, personas, lookahead.
Background road traffic is a PLACEHOLDER fraction of capacity (HPMS not wired), lowered now that inbound commuters are modeled.

Inbound commuters (home outside the box): only the in-box part of their trip is routed on the network; the approach outside the box (drive to a gateway, or walk/drive to a MARTA station) is an ESTIMATE added to their minutes. Their drawn paths start where they enter the box. Outbound commuters are not modeled.
Mode choice: one global constant calibrated to a PLACEHOLDER 12% transit share (ACS mode share not wired).

Equity inputs: ACS 2024 5-year (B25003, B19013, B25064, B25070), Census 2023 tract boundaries, HOLC 1938 Atlanta (Mapping Inequality, Univ. of Richmond). Agent 'renter' is SAMPLED from the home tract's renter share (seeded), not observed. displacementRisk is not modeled ('none').

approval.note: From display-sample stake scores: minutes delta, noise zone, and rent-pressure exposure of sampled renters (cost share not yet in the score).

personas.name: Tasha
personas.descriptor: Commutes to Georgia Tech · renter in Cabbagetown
personas.quote: My trip to Georgia Tech goes from 57 to 39 minutes. That's real time back every morning.
cannedReplies: By the model's numbers my commute is 57 minutes today and 39 minutes with the line.
My block isn't in the rent-pressure zone, so rent isn't my main worry.
I'm not near the construction zone.
I'd pay about $30 a year toward it either way.
